evidence.quote: Let $X$ be a real Banach space.

outputs.exact_statement:
Each of the four completed spaces $X_K$ is a separable infinite-dimensional real Banach space. For $K\in\{K_{\rm s},K_{\rm p},K_{\rm a},K_{\rm g}\}$ and $0<t<1$, $$\label{eq:common-bound}
 \widehat\delta_{X_K}(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1.$$ None of these spaces admits an equivalent AUC norm.

Let $X$ be a real Banach space. Suppose $0<m\le M<\infty$ and $c>0$, and, for every integer $h\ge1$, $X$ contains a tree $(p_s)_{s\in\mathbb N^{\le h}}$ with $m\le\|p_s\|\le M$. For every nonterminal $s$, suppose the child increments $d_{s,n}=p_{s^\frown n}-p_s$ are weakly null as $n\to\infty$ and $\|d_{s,n}\|\ge c$. If $N$ is an equivalent norm with $\alpha\|\cdot\|\le N\le\beta\|\cdot\|$ for constants $0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty$, then $\overline\delta_N(\alpha c/(2\beta M))=0$.
The real Banach space $X_{\mathrm e}$ defined by [fr:tests] and [fr:norm] satisfies $$\widehat\delta_{\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm e}}(t) \ge\frac{\sqrt{1+t^2/576}-1}{4}\qquad(0

The space $X_n=(H_n,L_n)$ is complete and $$\frac{\|x\|_2}{\sqrt{n+1}}\le L_n(x)\le\|x\|_2,
 \qquad
 L_n(x)=\sup_{p_n(f)\le1}\langle f,x\rangle.$$ Every coordinate satisfies $|x_s|\le L_n(x)$. Its continuous dual is $H_n$, under the Hilbert pairing, with norm $p_n$. In particular $L_n$ is exactly the global test norm on $T_n$.

The space $X$ is reflexive, has separable dual, and its dual is the Hilbert sum of the spaces $(H_n,p_n)$, with pairing $$f(x)=\sum_n\langle f_n,x_n\rangle,
 \qquad \|f\|_*^2=\sum_np_n(f_n)^2.$$ Every coordinate vector $e_{n,s}$ and every root path $b_{n,s}$ has norm one. For fixed $n$ and $|s|<n$, the children $(e_{n,s^\frown j})_{j\ge1}$ are weakly null. If $\alpha\|\cdot\|\le N\le\beta\|\cdot\|$, with $0<\alpha\le\beta$, then $\overline\delta_N(t)=0$ for every $0<t\le\alpha/\beta$. In particular no equivalent norm on $X$ is asymptotically uniformly convex.

Let $A$ be a finite head. Suppose $h,g\in X^*$ have norms at most one and $P_Ah=h$. There are $r_1,r_2\in X^*$, vanishing on $A$, such that $$r_1-r_2=(I-P_A)g,\qquad \|r_l\|_*\le2,
 \qquad
 \|\lambda h+\mu r_l\|_*^2\le\lambda^2+4\mu^2$$ for $l=1,2$ and $\lambda,\mu\ge0$.

Let $x\in X$ and let $(y_j)$ be a bounded weakly null sequence in $X$. If $L=\liminf_j\|y_j\|$, then $$\liminf_j\max\{\|x+y_j\|,\|x-y_j\|\}
 \ge\sqrt{\|x\|^2+L^2/16}.$$
If $0\le\nu\le\mu$ in $\ell_1(U)$, then $L_U(B_U\nu)\le L_U(B_U\mu)$.

On a forest of finite height, let $\mu,
u$ be nonnegative finitely supported endpoint masses. For a vertex $v$, let $K_v$ be its descendant set, and put $G(v)=\mu(K_v)$, $W(v)=
u(K_v)$. There is $0\leho\le\mu$ such that $$ho(K_v)\ge\min\{G(v),W(v)\}\quad\hbox{for every }v,
 \qquad \|ho\|_1\le\|
u\|_1.$$ The last inequality also holds separately in each tree of the forest.

Let $S\subseteq T\subset T_n$ be finite initial sets, let $z^+,z^-\in H_n$, and put $z=(z^++z^-)/2$. Put $U=T\setminus S$ and $$g=\tfrac12\big(V_T(z^+)+V_T(z^-)\big)-V_S(z).$$ Then $g\ge0$ and, for either sign, $$\label{eq:linear-mass-removal}
 L_n(R_Uz^\pm)\le2\|R_Uz\|_2+4g.$$
Under all hypotheses of Theorem 16, $$\label{eq:linear-energy-252} \sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E\|R_{\Delta_i}x_i\|^2\le252C^2.$$ In particular the bound is $1008$ when $\|x_m\|\le2$.

There is an absolute constant $K$ with the following property. Let $x_t=\mathbb E_t x_m$, $0\le t\le m$, be an $X$-valued dyadic martingale. For $0\le t<m$, let $A_t\subseteq D_t$ be finite initial sets measurable with respect to $\mathcal F_t$, and suppose $D_t\subseteq A_{t+1}$ whenever $t+1<m$. Put $U_t=D_t\setminus A_t$. Then $$\label{eq:linear-sign-energy}
 \sum_{t=0}^{m-1}\mathbb E\|R_{U_t}x_{t+1}\|^2
 \le K\left(\mathbb E\|x_m\|^2+
                  \sum_{t=0}^{m-1}\mathbb E\|R_{U_t}x_t\|^2\right).$$ No support condition on $x_t$ is imposed.

Let $W_i=\mathbb E_iW_m$, $0\le i\le m$, be an $X$-valued dyadic martingale. Let $A_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq A_m$ be fixed finite initial sets and put $\Delta_i=A_i\setminus A_{i-1}$. Then $$\label{eq:linear-leakage-1024}
 \sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E\|R_{\Delta_i}W_i\|^2
 \le1024\left(\mathbb E\|W_m\|^2+
              \sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E\|R_{\Delta_i}W_{i-1}\|^2\right).$$

The operator $R_A$ which sends the mass $\lambda_t$ to $r(t)$ and discards it when $r(t)=\perp$ is contractive on $L$. Moreover $$P_AJ=JR_A,\qquad \|P_A\|\le1,\qquad \|Q_A\|\le2,
 \qquad |Q_AJ_n\lambda|_n\le2\|\lambda\|_1.$$ Here the last formula is in a single component. In particular the path $p_t-p_{r(t)}$ outside the head has norm at most two.

No equivalent norm on $X_{\mathrm q}$ is asymptotically uniformly convex. More precisely, if $a\|z\|_{\mathrm q}\le N(z)\le b\|z\|_{\mathrm q}$, with $0<a\le b<\infty$, then $\overline\delta_N(t_0)=0$ at $t_0=a/(\sqrt2 b)$.

Let $O=T_n\setminus A_n$, let $\mathcal R$ be the roots of its connected subtrees, and suppose $V:O\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $$V(t)\ge\sum_{c\text{ child of }t}V(c),\qquad
 B:=\sum_{c\in\mathcal R}V(c)<\infty.$$ For any signs $\varepsilon_t$ constant on each connected subtree of $O$, the vector $\varepsilon_tV(t)$ on $O$, extended by zero on $A_n$, has norm at most $2B$ in $Z_n$. The pointwise minimum of two arrays satisfying the child inequality also satisfies it.

Let $A$ be a finite ancestral head in $X_{\mathrm q}$ and let $P_Ax=x$. For every $y\in X_{\mathrm q}$ and $R\ge0$, $$\label{qp:tail-eight}
 \|x+y\|_{\mathrm q},\ \|x-y\|_{\mathrm q}\le R
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|Q_Ay\|_{\mathrm q}\le8\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|_{\mathrm q}^2}.$$ The displacement $y$ need not vanish on the head.

If $x\in X_{\mathrm q}$ and an infinite sequence $(y_j)$ satisfies $\|x\pm y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\le R$ and $\|y_i-y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\ge\varepsilon>0$ for $i\ne j$, then $$\|x\|_{\mathrm q}^2+\frac{\varepsilon^2}{256}\le R^2.$$
If $\|x\pm y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\le r$ and $\|y_i-y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\ge2d>0$ for $i\ne j$ in an infinite sequence, then $$\|x\|_{\mathrm q}^2+d^2/144\le r^2.$$
Under the hypotheses of Theorem 26, $$\|Q_Ay\|_{\mathrm q}\le7\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|_{\mathrm q}^2}.$$
For $0<c\le1$ put $\delta=c^2/2000$. If $\|x\pm y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\le1$ and $\|y_i-y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\ge2c$ for all distinct indices of an infinite sequence, then $\|x\|_{\mathrm q}\le1-\delta$.
Under the hypotheses of Theorem 26, $$\|Q_Ay\|_{\mathrm q}\le9\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|_{\mathrm q}^2}.$$

For every $\rho>0$, choose $0<\gamma<1/2$ such that $$9\sqrt{(1+\gamma)^2-(1-2\gamma)^2}<\rho/3.$$ If $\|x\|_{\mathrm q}\ge1-\gamma$, its symmetric lens $\{y:\|x\pm y\|_{\mathrm q}\le1\}$ has no infinite $\rho$-separated subset.

Let $A\subset T_n$ be a finite nonempty ancestral head, with $P_Ax=x$, $P_Ay=0$, and $|x|_n=1$. If $0\le e\le1$ and $|x\pm y|_n\le1+e$, then $$\label{qp:rec:component-bound}
 |y|_n\le(6+\sqrt2)\sqrt{(1+e)^2-1}\le13\sqrt e.$$

Let $x\in X_{\mathrm q}$ be a unit vector with finite coordinate support. For each $n$ with $x_n\ne0$, choose a finite nonempty ancestor-closed $A_n\subset T_n$ containing its support, and set $$Y_x=\{y\in X_{\mathrm q}:P_{A_n}y_n=0
                           \text{ whenever }x_n\ne0\}.$$ Then $Y_x$ is a closed finite-codimensional subspace. If $0<e\le1/8$, $y\in Y_x$, and $\|x+y\|_{\mathrm q},\|x-y\|_{\mathrm q}\le1+e$, then $$\label{qp:rec:outer-bound}
 \|y\|_{\mathrm q}^2\le\frac{519}{2}e^{1/3},
 \qquad \|y\|_{\mathrm q}\le17e^{1/6}.$$

The costs are monotone, positively homogeneous and subadditive. On $\mathcal T_n$ they satisfy $$\label{sm:s:cost-comparisons}
 \|m\|_2\le M_n(m)
 \le\sum_{d=0}^{n}\|m|_{\mathbb N^d}\|_2
 \le\sqrt{n+1}\,\|m\|_2,
 \qquad
 \sum_{t\preceq v}m_t\le M_n(m).$$ For nonnegative forest arrays of finite total cost, $$\label{sm:s:positive-energy}
 M(m+r)^2\ge M(m)^2+M(r)^2.$$

For every node $v$ and $x\in X_S$, $|x_v|\le\|x\|_S$. The coordinate vector $e_v$ and every root-to-node path vector have norm one. If $C$ is a finite ancestral subset of $\mathcal T$, then its coordinate projection $P_C$ is contractive and $\|I-P_C\|\le2$. For a nonterminal node $t$, the sequence of its child coordinate vectors is weakly null.
The unit ball of $X_{\mathrm I}$ is the norm-closed convex hull of the atoms [sm:i:atoms]. In particular, finite linear combinations of the coordinate evaluations are dense in $X_{\mathrm I}$.
The real reflexive space $X_{\mathrm I}$ admits no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm.

For every finite prefix-closed $E$, both $P_E$ and $Q_E$ act contractively on $Y_{\mathrm I}$ and, by adjoints, on $X_{\mathrm I}$. On $X_{\mathrm I}$, $P_E$ has finite rank and retains exactly the coordinates indexed by $E$. For every $x\in X_{\mathrm I}$ and every $\eta>0$, there is such an $E$ with $\|Q_E x\|_{\mathrm I}<\eta$.

Let $E\subset\mathcal T$ be finite and prefix closed. If $x,y\in X_{\mathrm I}$ satisfy $$P_E x=x,\qquad \|x+y\|_{\mathrm I}\leq1,
 \qquad \|x-y\|_{\mathrm I}\leq1,$$ then $$\|Q_Ey\|_{\mathrm I}
 \leq (\sqrt2+\sqrt6)\sqrt{1-\|x\|_{\mathrm I}}.
 \label{sm:i:tail-bound}$$ In particular, if $Q_Ey=y$, the same bound holds for $\|y\|_{\mathrm I}$.

Let $0<c\leq1$ and let $x,u_j\in X_{\mathrm I}$, $j\in\mathbb N$, satisfy $$\|x+u_j\|_{\mathrm I},\ \|x-u_j\|_{\mathrm I}\leq1,
 \qquad \|u_j-u_k\|_{\mathrm I}\geq2c\quad(j\ne k).$$ Then, with $K=\sqrt2+\sqrt6$, $$\|x\|_{\mathrm I}\leq1-(c/K)^2<1.
 \label{sm:i:separation-bound}$$
